name: Chengdu Street Perception: Six Scales from 1 to 6
description:
Method replication: participants rate 25 Chengdu street views on six perceptions (safe, lively, boring, wealthy, depressing, beautiful), each from 1 to 6; the images are not the paper's stimuli (82 newly fetched Baidu street views inside Chengdu's Third Ring Road, one direction per point, cropped to remove the camera car).

Original study: Huang & Lee (2025), Journal of Asian Architecture and Building Engineering 24(5), 4470–4485. From Baidu street views along OSM roads inside Chengdu's Third Ring Road, 1,000 well-separated images were split into 10 groups of 100. 50 volunteers familiar with the city, in 10 groups of 5, each rated their group's 100 images on the six dimensions on a 1–6 scale (higher = fits better), so each image had about five ratings. Random forests predicted the scores for the whole area; PCA combined them and they were compared with street accessibility.

Differences from the original study: (1) 25 random images per participant instead of a fixed group of 100; (2) the end labels "1 = not at all" and "6 = very much" are written for this template; (3) familiarity with Chengdu is asked in one question instead of being a recruitment criterion.
author: Huang & Lee
